  3. engine/unicode (ucd)

#engine/unicode (ucd)

Odin port of QuickJS-ng's libunicode. It provides the Unicode data the regexp engine and the JS lexer need: character-set intervals, case conversion / folding / the ECMAScript regexp canonicalize, the identifier and whitespace predicates, the \p{} property / general-category / script sets, and the four normalization forms.

The package is named ucd (not unicode) so it does not collide with core:unicode. Import it with an alias:

Odin
import ucd "wb:engine/unicode"

It compiles for windows_amd64, linux_amd64 and freestanding_wasm32. Nothing in the runtime path touches the OS; every allocation goes through a caller-supplied allocator (pass an arena to free a whole build at once). The only hosted-only file is settings.odin (the preference registry needs an OS); it is excluded from the freestanding build with a #+build tag.

#Data: generated, pinned, never copied

The tables are generated from the authoritative Unicode Character Database, not copied from QuickJS's libunicode-table.h:

  • tools/gen_unicode.ps1 downloads the pinned UCD files for a fixed Unicode release (17.0.0, the version QuickJS-ng 0.17 ships), verifies each file's SHA-256 (the same idiom as tools/build_js.ps1), then runs the generator.
  • src/engine/unicode/gen/ (an Odin program) parses the UCD text and writes tables_generated.odin: sorted half-open interval runs for every property / category / script, simple and full case/fold tables, and the decomposition / combining-class / composition tables for normalization.
  • src/engine/unicode/tables_generated.odin is committed so a normal build needs no network. Re-run the script to move to another Unicode release; the pinned version shows up as the unicode.version preference.

#Char_Range and set operations

Char_Range is a set of code points stored as a sorted, non-overlapping list of half-open [lo, hi) intervals on a caller-chosen allocator. It is the v-flag set-notation primitive and the shape every property lookup fills.

Odin
cr: ucd.Char_Range
ucd.cr_init(&cr, allocator)
defer ucd.cr_destroy(&cr)
ucd.general_category(&cr, "Lu")          // fill with uppercase letters
ucd.cr_op_inplace(&cr, &other, .Inter)   // union / inter / xor / sub
ucd.cr_invert(&cr)                        // complement within [0, 0x110000)
in_set := ucd.cr_contains(&cr, 'A')

#Case, canonicalize, predicates

Odin
ucd.simple_case(c, .To_Upper | .To_Lower | .Fold) -> u32          // 1:1
ucd.full_case(&res3, c, conv) -> int                               // 1..3 code points
ucd.canonicalize(c, is_unicode) -> u32                             // ECMAScript regexp i-flag rule
ucd.cr_canonicalize(&cr, is_unicode)                               // canonicalize a whole class
ucd.is_id_start / is_id_continue / is_white_space / is_cased / is_case_ignorable
ucd.js_is_ident_first / js_is_ident_next                           // lexer rule: ID_* plus $ _ ZWNJ ZWJ

is_id_start/is_id_continue return the raw Unicode property (matching QuickJS's lre_is_*). The lexer-level helpers add $, _, ZWNJ and ZWJ.

#Normalization

Odin
out := ucd.normalize(src_codepoints, .NFC | .NFD | .NFKC | .NFKD, allocator)

Standard algorithm: recursive canonical/compat decomposition, canonical ordering by combining class, then canonical composition for the C forms, with the algorithmic Hangul rules built in.

#Checking it

tools/rx_diff.ps1 builds a native reference library from QuickJS-ng 0.17's libunicode.c and compares this package against it over every code point and thousands of random normalization inputs. See docs/engine/regexp.md for the results. The UCD pin follows QuickJS-ng (17.0.0) so the identifier, case-folding and property data agree with the reference engine.
